overview: In the King's Gambit Accepted White plays 3.Be2 (the Lesser Bishop's Gambit) rather than 3.Nf3 or 3.Bc4, planning Nf3, Bxf4, O-O and d4. Black can keep the pawn with ...Nf6, ...d5 or the sharper 3...f5 (Weiss Defence). White has a pawn deficit for central control and an open f-file.

white_ideas.idea: Win back f4 with Nf3, Bxf4
Castle and use the half-open f-file

black_ideas.idea: Counterattack in the centre with ...d5 or ...f5

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with White pawn deficit on f4

character.notes: The King's Gambit family: material tension and quick development.

gambit.notes: The f-pawn is given up and Black can keep it with ...d5 or ...Nf6.

soundness.notes: A sound and slightly slower gambit; not refuted.

structure.notes: Open centre once exd5 or exf5 occurs.

approach.notes: A side branch that strong players play occasionally; I treat it as standard.

level.notes: Needs known lines and trap awareness.

sublines_that_differ.name: Weiss Defence
sublines_that_differ.how: A sharper reply and a separate named line

character.reason: King's Gambit positions are tactical with an exposed white king.

gambit.reason: White gives up the f-pawn and Black can keep it.

soundness.reason: Playable gambit without a known refutation.

structure.reason: The centre opens fast with exd5 or exf5.
